markets.note: Shown for contrast only. Market prices are never an input to this model: traders read forecasts, so using them would be circular.

events.title: Which party will win the Senate in 2026?
Republican Senate seats after the 2026 midterm elections?

rivals.note: Other published forecasts of the same question, each read on the date shown. Hand-entered from the source page, because none of them publishes a feed. They are never an input to this model.

forecasters.note: '99 out of 100'; median outcome D+51, 243 seats. Page states 'LAST UPDATED: OCT 25 AT 3:10PM'. Unchanged from 2026-10-10.

forecasters.name: Silver Bulletin
forecasters.note: Free preview states Democrats' House chances are 'up to nearly 94 percent' in the FLIPR Deluxe model. Prose, not a published figure, so 0.94 is approximate. No Senate number was public this week -- the reverse of 2026-09-14, when the Senate was free and the House paid.

forecasters.name: ElectIt
forecasters.note: Harvard/Caltech LogisTiCC model (Ebanks, Katz, King). 'Model + All Polls' variant, the only one using district and state polls and so the only one comparable to this model. 240 seats, 95% range [211,283]; national House vote D 54.0%. Polls last updated 2026-10-25 02:01 ET.

forecasters.name: Poliwave
forecasters.note: 'Updated Oct 25, 2026', 100,000 simulations. 230 seats, 217-248 in 80% of runs -- an 80% range, so it is not recorded in the p05/p95 columns, which are 90%. The site states its probabilities 'have not been calibrated against past elections'.

forecasters.name: DDHQ
forecasters.note: Page states 'Last updated Oct 24, 8:24 PM'; 80% and a 237-198 seat split, flagged as up over one week. Topline is rendered graphically, read from the page.
